newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end uneventful pit trading mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end uneventful pit trading mixed.

text.p: Uneventful afternoon pit trading left U.S. interest rates futures mixed and barely changed from Tuesday's settlements.
Futures drifted during the latter part of the session after recovering from a morning pullback to day's lows.
Traders said one house was seen as a featured buyer of at least 3,000 September Treasury bond futures on the move back up that tugged the contract to the day's high.
But the rise lacked muscle to drive futures above 110-05/32, just as the morning's drop failed to punch below support at the 200-day moving average near 109-22/32 - 23/32.

They agreed that many technicals still pointed to price strength nearterm. But ambivalence about what Friday's May U.S. jobs report will reveal kept prices tethered to familiar ranges Wednesday and discouraged even professional traders.

"Technically, it's really strong," said one Eurodollar floor trader. "Bonds are firm and they had closed above their channel line...I'd like to sell it" but did not expect to find much opportunity before the jobs data.
Economists expect nonfarm payrolls to rise 219,000, with a 5.0-percent jobless rate, a 0.4-percent gain in average hourly earnings and an average workweek of 34.7 hours.
The new estimates were compiled June 3 after the U.S. Labor Department released revised seasonal factors last week.

September T-bond futures dipped to the day's low when two dealers sold roughly 2,500 apiece, sales that brokers figured represented hedges stemming from Brazil's 30-year global bond and Brady buyback offer, which expired on Tuesday.
Pressure also stemmed from the 1.2-percent rise in April U.S. factory orders versus forecasts for up 0.8 percent.
Futures showed muted response to morning comments by St Louis Federal Reserve Bank president Thomas Melzer and afternoon remarks by Minneapolis Fed president Gary Stern.
Melzer said persistently high money growth and not economic growth is what causes high inflation.
Stern said the economy is growing at a steady pace with few, if any, hints of serious trouble spots at the moment.

September T-bonds settled down 2/32 at 110-01/32, 10-year notes ended flat at 107-10/32, munis rose 5/32 to 116-02/32, Sept T-bills lost 0.005 to 94.650, and Dec Eurodollars ended unchanged at 93.795. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
